lines: A stranger in the Hollow, a new face on the green! Welcome, friend, welcome, to the cosiest town you've seen!
{player}: Did you just make that up?
I make everything up! I'm Barnaby, the town troubadour. Songs for every occasion. And some for no occasion.
(He's strumming a jolly tune about a snowman who wanted to see the summer.)
This next one's called 'The Hum Beneath the Oak'. I wrote it. I don't know why. It just... came to me one midnight.
(He's strumming a jolly tune about a pumpkin who wanted to be a moon.)
This next one's called 'The Hum Beneath the Oak'. I wrote it. I don't know why. It just... came to me one midnight.
Listen... the old oak's humming again. It always gets louder near midnight. Like it's tuning up for something.
Last week I saw a green flicker down there, right at twelve. Then Mr. Palmer walked out of the trees, cool as you like, and said 'evening'.
(He's singing a soft song about a sleepy pond and a duck called Gerald.)
Shh, Gerald's listening. He's my biggest fan.
On a clear night you can see every star from up here. And sometimes... one more. Just past the old oak. It flickers green.
Green as a pickle! Must write a song about it.
(Strum!) Good morning, good morning, the snow is soft and white! Good morning, good morning, and Gus is grumpy, right!
(From across the street, someone yells "I HEARD THAT".)
(Strum!) Good morning, good morning, the leaves are turning gold! Good morning, good morning, and Gus is being cold!
(From across the street, someone yells "I HEARD THAT".)

rotate: Want a request? I know every song. Except the one about the moose. Nobody knows that one. It's too sad.
Gus once paid me five dollars to play somewhere else. I played in front of the diner. It's somewhere else!
(He plays a twinkly little tune.) That's my winter song. It's called 'The Snowflake Who Was Scared Of Heights'.
The festival's my big night! I'm playing the whole evening. Bring earmuffs! Joking. Bring dancing shoes.
